Subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, SCC module suggestion & next steps (Northbound Labs)

Hi Priya / Kevin — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so legal/privacy can kick off cleanly: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: Northbound will send customer‑facing prompts and get generated outputs to display in product UI.
- Data flows: user-provided text + metadata stored for 30 days for troubleshooting; no healthcare PHI expected in initial rollout.
- Compliance asks: confirmation of SOC 2 status, DPA + SCC selection, and whether Redwood is processor or has any joint-controller surface (logs/analytics).

Redwood suggested posture (initial recommendation)
- Controller/Processor: Redwood standard approach is to act as Processor for hosted inference; we can discuss limited joint-controller behavior for customer analytics if you plan to ingest Northbound’s telemetry into Redwood-managed observability.
- SCC/DPA: recommend SCC Module 2 (processor-transfer focused) with a DPA that includes a narrow logging addendum covering retention and access controls.
- SOC 2: we can share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.

Immediate next steps
1) Please share your vendor security questionnaire and any DPA redline (if you have one) — we’ll start triaging.
2) Karthik will confirm the Processor/Controller boundary for the logging/analytics callouts and propose wording for the DPA addendum.
3) We’ll deliver initial VSQ answers and SOC 2 evidence within 3 business days of receiving your VSQ.

Attachments referenced: none yet — Priya, if you have the VSQ, please send it across.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA scope, SCC module suggestion & next steps (Northbound Labs)

Priya — thanks for sending the VSQ and the DPA redline. Quick technical/legal posture from Redwood: 

- Processor vs Joint Controller: Redwood’s default for hosted API and hosted model inference is Processor. We are willing to evaluate narrow joint‑controller language only where Northbound requires Redwood to independently decide on purposes/means (e.g., if Redwood were to enrich Northbound data with third‑party signals). For your telemetry case (conversation IDs + anonymized error traces used strictly for service reliability), that typically stays within Processor boundaries; Northbound would remain the party that decides retention windows and legal basis for end‑user data.

- SCC module: for a U.S. company transferring EU data, the typical fit is the SCC set that covers Processor transfers (SCC Module 2 in the 2021 framework). Because your DPA redline includes access to logs and extended retention clauses, I recommend: SCC Module 2 (processor) + a narrow DPA addendum that explicitly states retention (30 days) and access controls (redwood support read-only access limited to specific role ids). That keeps cross-border transfer language clear while addressing your legal ask.

- VSQ: we’ll start answering the VSQ today. Expect a prioritized answers pack (high‑risk items first) within 48–72 hours.

Next steps (from Redwood legal/engineering)
1) We will produce suggested DPA language for the telemetry logging addendum and send it as a tracked redline.
2) We will complete the initial VSQ response (48–72 hours).
3) If Northbound insists on joint‑controller language, we’ll schedule a short call with our privacy counsel to discuss scope and residual risk (likely adds 1–2 weeks).

If helpful, I can include sample wording here in the thread — e.g., a short clause: 
"For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood acts as Processor with respect to customer prompt data and generated outputs, and processes logs and telemetry on behalf of Northbound for the sole purpose of service operation and troubleshooting; retention limited to 30 days unless otherwise agreed in writing."

—Karthik

- Suggested SCC approach: Processor transfer SCC (Module 2) + DPA addendum covering logging retention (30 days) and role-based access controls.

Deliverables and timing:
- Redwood to upload SOC 2 Type II (2025) PDF to a secure link: by EOD Friday (we will provide a secure download link).
- Karthik to circulate a tracked redline DPA addendum for telemetry by EOD Friday.
- Redwood engineering/legal to provide prioritized VSQ answers within 72 hours of receiving the XLS (we have today to start).

Ask from Northbound: please confirm whether the 30‑day retention window is acceptable and whether you need any extended retention for specific integrations (if so, list which ones). Also confirm who at Northbound should receive the SOC 2 link (security@northboundlabs.com is fine).

I’ll follow up with the secure SOC2 link and the initial DPA redline.

Hannah
